clue.text: Six hours during which payments fall due

definitions.text: Six hours during which payments fall due

parts.words: Six hours during which payments fall due
parts.note: six hours is a fourth part of a twenty-four-hour stretch, and the traditional English rent days fell on such named dates each season

explanation.surface: A short window in which bills must be settled.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'six hours' literally as a fraction of a whole day; the same phrase names the four fixed dates in the English calendar when rents and dues were paid.
explanation.definitionFit: The English legal calendar has four fixed days each year when rents were payable, and a quarter of a day is six hours.

clue.text: Find fault in missile

definitions.meaning: to complain or dispute, as a verb
a short heavy bolt shot from a crossbow

explanation.surface: Discovering a defect in a rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue or take issue with, and a square-headed crossbow bolt.

clue.text: Here you'll find craft are moored higgledy-piggledy

indicators.note: higgledy-piggledy means in a jumbled mess, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A harbour where boats are tied up in a jumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' and 'moored' suggest boats; the craft are aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: An airfield is a place where aircraft are kept and take off.

clue.text: Cosmetic surgeon might show disdain thus

definitions.meaning: a plastic surgeon could literally tilt the tip of a nose upward

explanation.surface: A plastic surgeon's sneer.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to sniff at something as beneath you, scorning it.

clue.text: Very large quantity to share out again

parts.note: real is used informally for very, as in real good
a lot is a large quantity

explanation.surface: Such a huge amount it must be divided up once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To reallot is to distribute or assign afresh.

clue.text: Tree has a conspirator moving right to the top

indicators.note: moving says one letter leaves its place in the conspirator's name
in a down clue the top is the start, so the letter goes to the front

parts.note: Brutus conspired to assassinate Julius Caesar

explanation.surface: A tree hides a plotter shifting to the upper branches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' with 'to the top' is a move, not a deletion: in a down entry the top is the start, so the R of Caesar's assassin's name shifts to the front (RBUTUS).
explanation.definitionFit: Arbutus is the strawberry tree, an evergreen shrub.

clue.text: Send back prisoners in exchange

indicators.note: sending something back returns it the way it came, so the word for prisoners is read backwards

parts.note: POWs are prisoners of war

explanation.surface: Captives are returned as part of a prisoner exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: A swap (also spelt with an O) is a trade of one thing for another.

clue.text: Confused unknowns brought to court

indicators.note: brought to means the unknowns are added on to the end of the courting word

parts.note: to woo is to court
x, y and z are unknowns in algebra; here two of them

explanation.surface: Puzzled strangers are summoned before a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks legal but is the verb to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: Woozy means dazed or muddled in the head.

clue.text: Carriage upset or crashed

indicators.note: crashed means wrecked and broken up, so these letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A coach overturned or smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' and 'upset' suggest a coach accident; carriage is bearing, how one holds oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage means the way a person holds their body, their bearing.

clue.text: Scorpion has this unexpectedly unpleasant end

definitions.meaning: a scorpion literally carries its venomous barb at the rear
a nasty surprise held back until the finish

explanation.surface: A scorpion's venomous barb sums up a nasty surprise ending.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a nasty twist saved for last, from the scorpion's barb.

clue.text: Horse runs beside river

indicators.note: beside puts the letter for runs immediately next to the river, after it here

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A racehorse gallops along a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' looks equine, but it is a clothes horse, the frame for drying laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes horse is a folding frame for drying washing, also called a drying rack.

clue.text: Flier rarely seen on course

definitions.meaning: a large seabird of the southern oceans with a huge wingspan
on a golf course, a score of three under par on one hole, which is very rare

explanation.surface: A bird that seldom turns up on the golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: The great seabird gives its name to the golfing score of three under par, a rare feat on any hole.

clue.text: Deter characters improperly catching island's fish

indicators.note: catching means the rearranged letters close round the island like a net
improperly says the letters of deter are not in their proper order

parts.note: the characters, or letters, of the word deter
Mull is an island in the Scottish Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: Letters wrongly arranged trap a fish from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'island's' might suggest IS or I, but here it is the Hebridean island; 'improperly' gives REDET, which 'catching' splits round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The red mullet is a reddish Mediterranean food fish, also called surmullet.

clue.text: This could get you drunk with an alcoholic drink

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling about, mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A liqueur strong enough to get you tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges YOU and AN; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Noyau is a brandy liqueur flavoured with fruit kernels, a sweet spirit.

clue.text: Crow's nest found in cave!

definitions.meaning: the platform high on a ship's mast where a watch is kept
Latin for beware, a British schoolboys' warning cry that a teacher is coming

explanation.surface: A bird's nest discovered in a cavern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cave' looks like a hollow in rock; it is the Latin warning 'cave!' (beware), old British school slang for 'watch out'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry post on a mast and a cry of warning both mean keeping watch for danger.

clue.text: Variety of pines, so thorny

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so these letters are given a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: One kind of pine tree is especially prickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinose is a botanical term for covered in spines, prickly.

clue.text: Run and fall

definitions.meaning: in cricket, an extra run scored when a fielder's throw goes past the stumps
a downfall or defeat, as of a government

explanation.surface: Sprinting and then tumbling over.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an errant return throw can give the batting side an extra run.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketing extra from a wild throw, and the toppling of a ruler or regime.

clue.text: Some interpret "extenuation" as "excuse"

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: People may read a plea of mitigation as nothing more than a way out.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'as'; the definition is just 'excuse', with 'as' a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretext is a false reason given to hide the real one, an alibi.

clue.text: Crime pieced together by those sitting in judgment

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
a jury sits to judge a case

explanation.surface: A jury pieces together the evidence of an offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieced together' signals that the answer is put together from pieces; it gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying under oath is an offence against justice.

clue.text: Transatlantic explorer set up business in Virginia, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue set up lifts the name so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: John Cabot sailed across the Atlantic to North America in 1497
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: An explorer from across the ocean founds a company in the American colony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virginia' looks like the US state; it is a variety of leaf grown there.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia is a type of leaf grown for smoking, an example of the crop.

clue.text: Conjecture about officer's retreat being cowardly

indicators.note: about means the word for conjecture goes around the other piece

parts.note: to guess is to conjecture

indicators.note: a retreat goes backwards, so the officer's letters are reversed

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: Speculation that an officer's withdrawal was a sign of cowardice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' looks like a noun for a hideaway, but it is the reversal signal, giving TL; 'about' wraps the conjecture word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no guts means lacking courage, so spineless or craven.

clue.text: Troublemaker bringing about change of leadership in foreign government

indicators.note: a change of leadership swaps the first letter, the leader, of the government word

parts.note: the Kremlin stands for the Russian government

explanation.surface: A mischief-maker brings about a coup abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A gremlin is an imaginary imp blamed for mechanical faults.

clue.text: Sprinkler and spades to, collect, say

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for spades in card games
a collect is a short prayer in church services

explanation.surface: Garden tools gathered up for watering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collect' looks like a verb; it is the noun, a short prayer said in church.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprayer is a device that scatters water in fine drops.

clue.text: European citizen's French book

definitions.meaning: a citizen of Rome, the Italian capital
the French word for a novel

explanation.surface: A European's novel written in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Italian capital, and the French word for a novel.

clue.text: One getting invested with medal by monarch — no speech from him

indicators.note: by means next to, so the monarch's letters follow
invested means clothed, so one is wrapped inside the medal letters

parts.note: MM is the Military Medal
I is the Roman numeral one
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A soldier receives a medal from the Queen, who says nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an investiture ceremony; the definition is a silent performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mime artist performs without words, only gestures.

clue.text: Carnivorous warder

definitions.meaning: a meat lover, someone who eats steak, read as describing them
a Yeoman Warder at the Tower of London

explanation.surface: A guard who loves his meat.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yeoman Warders who guard the Tower of London are nicknamed this; split the word and it is someone who eats steak.
explanation.definitionFit: Tower of London guards carry this nickname, and taken literally it is one who eats meat from cattle.

clue.text: Tone-deaf MC in usual tizzy

indicators.note: a tizzy is a state of flustered confusion, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A master of ceremonies flustered in his normal way can't carry a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but is part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tone-deaf has no ear for music.

clue.text: Show Australian river flowing the wrong way

indicators.note: a river flowing the wrong way runs backwards, so its name is read in reverse

parts.note: the Yarra is the river through Melbourne

explanation.surface: A display of an Australian river running backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An array is an impressive display, a show of things laid out.

clue.text: Story that's long, lacking a point

indicators.note: lacking means the word for long is missing the point

parts.note: to long for is to yearn
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A tale that goes on and on without a purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A yarn is a long rambling tale, a tall story.

clue.text: Plant that can provide fine meal, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: cornflour is a fine starch meal ground from maize

explanation.surface: A crop from which a fine meal can be made.
explanation.definitionFit: The blue-flowered field plant is a common cottage garden bloom.
